group: Public pages — marketing site, try-it pages, events and public links

modules.name: The marketing website (openmaison.ai)
modules.what: OpenMaison's public website, redesigned in June 2026 ('The Quiet Operating System'). It has a home page, a Platform hub with 8 module pages (AI Visualiser, Space Planner, Quote Digitizer, Finance & Margins, Leads, Projects, Meeting Co-pilot, mAIson bot), Story, Trust & Security, a Blog (21 articles kept in code), What's New (about 30 changelog entries), Jobs (4 roles, apply by email), Contact, Privacy, Terms and Cookies. 'Book a demo' asks for name, studio, email and phone, saves them, then opens Calendly. The footer's newsletter box saves emails. The contact form saves the message and emails hello@openmaison.ai. Every page carries SEO metadata, structured data, a sitemap, robots rules and a branded link-preview picture (/api/og). Pricing is hidden before launch (it redirects home). /about, /products and /ai-agents redirect to the newer pages. A separate UAE campaign page (/uae-get-started) has its own free-trial form.

modules.name: Try-it pages (AI Visualizer trial)
modules.what: An AI Visualizer trial for visitors who are not signed in. A visitor uploads a room photo (or picks a sample) and uses the real editor's tools: style, materials (tap a surface to swap its finish), lighting, furniture, defurnish (empty the room) and sketch-to-render. Each browser gets 3 free renders (counted in a signed cookie). Renders use the Fast model only and carry a watermark. After that comes 'Sign up free' → onboarding. Six per-tool pages carry their own search-engine copy. The older /try page offers pre-rendered sample rooms and styles plus one live restyle of your own photo.
modules.where_in_1: /try-visualizer and /try-visualizer/{style, materials, lighting, furniture, defurnish, sketch} — reached from the website's Platform › AI Visualiser 'Try Now'; /try (older demo, linked from nowhere)

modules.name: Hangouts (meet-the-designer events)
modules.what: Qanvast Hangouts are in-person events where homeowners meet several interior designers at tables in one venue. On their phone at /hangouts/[eventId], a homeowner signs in with an SMS code, gives their preferences (property type and status, budget, key collection, region, style) and waits while staff match them. They then see the day's meetings, each with the designer's profile and portfolio, start each meeting, and read AI insights after it. Voucher rewards at 4, 5 and 6 meetings are shown locked (payouts paused). Staff run the event from Admin › Hangouts. They create events with shifts and a venue, approve studios and their designers, and register homeowners. Matching uses a 0–100 preference score. They also have a live table board (refreshed every 5 s), outcomes per meeting (converted · follow-up · dropped), analytics, and recording / transcript downloads with retry.

modules.name: Client links that open without signing in
modules.what: The links a studio sends a client or vendor, which open without an account. They cover signing (/sign/[token]), the quote (/quote/[token] behind an SMS code, and /quote-preview/[token], a live read-only view), payments (/pay/[token], the old project portal; /pay/inv/[token] an invoice; /pay/receipt/[token] a receipt), purchase orders (/po/[token]), designs (/renders/[token]), the 3-D floor plan (/floor-plan/view/[token]), the client portal (/my/...), the meeting brief (/copilot/share/[shareId]) and the X-Ray (/sign/quote-xray/[token]).
modules.in_2: Almost all of it. Signing: /sign/[id], /sign/bundle/[id], /sign/[id]/quote. The quote's confirmation: /confirm/[quoteId]. Money: /invoice/[token], /receipt/[token]. Purchase orders: /po/[token]. Designs: /renders/[token]. 3-D layouts: /space/[token]. Shared files: /f/[token]. The client portal /my/[slug] covers Home, Schedule, Updates, Money (invoice and receipt), Choices, Designs, Floor plan, Issues, Messages and About.
pending: Links from 1.0 already in clients' WhatsApp threads have nowhere to land in 2.0. The projects migration map's D-11 (send /pay/…, /pay/inv/…, /pay/receipt/… and /my/{slug}/p/… to the portal's sign-in) is waiting on him.

A read-only 'have a look' quote link: 1.0's /quote-preview/[token] (from the Quote Digitizer's Share) updates live as the studio edits. In 2.0 the client gets the quote only through Send for confirmation (/confirm) or the signing link.

A real SMS code before a client link opens. 1.0's old payment portal never actually sends its code, and the quote link's code screen has no generator mounted. 2.0's portal accepts any six digits (a stand-in). This is developers' work.
A picture card when the link is pasted into WhatsApp. 2.0's design link has one. Its signing, confirm, invoice, receipt and PO links show their title only, where 1.0 showed the website's card. Small.
The meeting brief link /copilot/share/[shareId] is held with Meetings (REG-552). The X-Ray's public link was decided no (X-Ray audit Q-24).
modules.depends_on: an SMS provider for real codes; his D-11 call on old links
modules.held_by: projects map D-11 (his call); REG-552 for the meeting brief link; X-Ray Q-24 (no public link)
modules.why: Everything a client sees is already built in 2.0, often more fully than in 1.0. What is left is porting work: old links landing somewhere sensible (his D-11 call first) and real SMS codes.

modules.name: Industry news feed
modules.what: /api/news pulls property and design news from regional RSS feeds (Singapore: PropertyGuru and others). It sorts the stories into property, design, regulation or market, scores how relevant each is, and caches them for an hour. Despite sitting among the public APIs, it feeds only the Dashboard home's news card, not the website.

modules.depends_on: RSS feeds per region; the Dashboard
modules.why: It only makes sense as a card on the Dashboard, which he has held. Decide it with the Dashboard.
